# CROSSWATER — client facts and archive records

## Project

- Project name: CROSSWATER.
- Project type: archive-based short-trip commuter passenger-cabin concept.
- Archive vessel: Ferry EUREKA, HAER CA-59.
- Design boundary: the complete enclosed passenger saloon between two transverse sliding-door partitions, including both sides of the central fixed bodies.
- Design language: contemporary or slightly ahead of the 2026 market; purposeful surfacing, considered lighting and modern materials and colours.
- Existing shell: fixed horizontal geometry and source-supported architectural relationships.
- New work: cabin arrangement, seating, standing places, handholds, bag storage, finishes and passenger information.
- Exterior end decks, toilet interiors, engines and shore infrastructure: retained context.

## Archive image records

| File | Record | Date | Content and provenance |
|---|---|---|---|
| 03-archive-plan.png | HAER CA-59 passenger-deck panel | 1998 | Faithful crop of Dana Lockett's HAER addendum; source drawings Tri-Coastal / DePavloff Co., May 1990 |
| 04-archive-photo18.png | HAER CA-59-18 | 1988 | Jet Lowe photograph toward the newsstand; reduced from the downloaded original TIFF |
| 05-archive-photo21.png | HAER CA-59-21 | 1988 | Jet Lowe photograph of athwartships passenger seating; encoding of the official 1920-pixel preview |

- All three archive images: the same vessel.
- Plan and photographs: records from different years.
- Horizontal positions: passenger-deck plan.
- Photographic information: visible architectural relationships.
- Exact camera positions and intervening alterations: unspecified in the supplied records.
- Original scale bar: below the plan crop at exactly the same reduction; feet descend from 40 at left to 0 at right.
- Centerline numbers including 35 and 40: frame/station identifiers.
- Horizontal conversion: 1 foot = 304.8 mm.
- Traced horizontal values: approximate archive-derived dimensions.
- Parent plan's Commons title: Title Sheet.
- Parent plan image and credit block: 1998 addendum.

## Fixed shell inventory

| Element | Fixed relationship |
|---|---|
| Outer saloon boundary | Traced archive outline |
| Window walls | Recorded opening rhythm |
| Transverse sliding-door partitions | Both saloon ends |
| Saloon door openings | Four total, two at each end; archived positions and widths |
| Support columns | Archive column dots |
| Kingposts | Archive positions |
| Engine casing/A-frame enclosure | Archive footprint |
| Newsstand enclosure | Fixed footprint; new informational surface available |
| Smokestack casing | Archive footprint |
| Storage-room partitions around smokestack casing | Archive positions |
| Restroom/storage partitions | Archive positions and access |
| Fire-main positions | Archive positions and visibility |
| Water fountain | Archive position |
| Exterior end decks | Recorded stairs, railings and boundary |

- Existing movable benches, tables and merchandise: replaceable layout context.
- Orientation: page-left = Oakland end; page-right = San Francisco end.
- End names: cabin orientation labels.
- Plan-relative side descriptions: upper edge and lower edge.
- P&S: port and starboard.
- T&G: tongue and groove.
- TYP: typical.
- UP: up.
- DN: down.

## Vertical information and section

- Existing cabin, door, sill, window-head, beam and ceiling heights: unmeasured in the supplied material.
- Existing vertical envelope: undimensioned.
- Existing overhead structure: retained architectural relationship.
- Section A-A location: open saloon between the Oakland-end partition and the newsstand.
- Section type: transverse relational section tied to the actual proposed plan cut.
- Section relationships: source-supported side windows, upper windows, posts and beams.
- Exact section caption: Relational section; existing heights unmeasured.
- Dimensioned section content: proposed seating, handholds and bag-storage elements.

## Layout and furniture targets

| Item | Quantity or dimension | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Seats | 120 | Proposed layout target |
| Two-person seating modules | 60 | Proposed layout target |
| Sitting surface per person | 480 mm wide × 440 mm deep | Nominal new-element dimensions |
| Sitting surface height | 450 mm above local floor | New-element dimension |
| Standing places | 24 | Separately marked proposed positions |
| Standing planning box | 550 × 550 mm | Nominal planning footprint |
| Handhold provision | One proposed hold available to each standing place | Layout relationship |
| Lower grasp surface | At least one at 950 mm above local floor | New-element dimension |
| Upper grasp surface | At least one at 1100 mm above local floor | New-element dimension |
| Bag positions | 12, numbered B01-B12 | Across one or more storage units |
| Upright sample bag | 300 mm wide × 200 mm deep × 450 mm high | One bag per numbered position |
| Full storage-detail case | 12 sample bags together | One complete storage arrangement |
| Circulation band | 1200 mm clear | Proposed continuous planning target |
| Existing door throats | Archived widths | Local exception to the circulation-band width |

- Seat back shape, armrests, legs and shell form: open design choices.
- Handhold routes and mounting design: proposed new work.
- Count record: complete cabin plan.
- Other views: the arrangement established by the cabin plan.
- Circulation connections: all four saloon door approaches, around both sides of the central fixed bodies.
- Furniture, standing boxes and bag positions: outside the circulation band.
- Door-leaf travel, fire-main positions and restroom/storage access: clear areas.

## Passenger cases

| Case | State | People | Bags | Printed wording |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CASE A, first moment | Vessel stationary; leaving at Oakland end | Three leaving passengers | Carried commuter bags as depicted | Alight first |
| CASE A, second moment | Vessel stationary; boarding at Oakland end | Three boarding passengers | Carried commuter bags as depicted | Then board |
| CASE B | Short ride | Six seated passengers and two standing passengers using proposed holds | Three bags in B01-B03 | Seating; Standing; Bags |

- CASE A order: first moment followed by second moment.
- Passenger counts: staged scene populations.
- Bag placement: storage or carried positions clear of circulation and door travel.
- People representation: diagrammatic figures or illustrated passengers.
- Video duration: 10 seconds.
- Video sequence: CASE A followed by CASE B.

## Materials and information

| Surface | Material assignment |
|---|---|
| New seat contact surfaces | Recycled PET upholstery |
| Supports and handholds | Aluminium |
| Bag-contact surfaces | Rubber liners |
| Floor and circulation cues | Rubber floor surfaces with integrated visual cues |
| Information panels | Printed aluminium |

- Colour palette and codes: design choices recorded on the material and colour system board.
- Zone differentiation: colour paired with words and distinct shapes.
- Window openings: retained visibility.
- Fire-main positions: retained visibility.
- Newsstand information-panel name: CROSSWATER.
- Exact passenger labels: Alight first; Then board; Seating; Standing; Bags; Oakland end; San Francisco end.
- Orientation labels: Oakland end and San Francisco end.
- Presentation length: at least 8 pages.

## Additional atmosphere input

- 06-waterfront-boarding-reference.png: contemporary waterfront boarding atmosphere with commuters, bags and a bicycle.
- Image role: reference.
- Source type: generated illustration.

## Archive credits and source records

- Institutional credit: Historic American Engineering Record, National Park Service, Library of Congress.
- Passenger plan: Dana Lockett, 1998.
- Source drawings: Tri-Coastal / DePavloff Co., May 1990.
- Photographs: Jet Lowe, 1988, HAER CA-59-18 and CA-59-21.
- Archive image rights: public-domain government documentation.
- Supplied archive image treatments: faithful crop, reduction or preview encoding.
- Presentation credit: one archive-credit entry distinguishing the 1998 plan, May 1990 source drawings and 1988 photographs.
- Primary identity: https://www.loc.gov/item/ca1504/
- Rights record: https://www.loc.gov/rr/print/res/114_habs.html
- Rights guidance: https://www.nps.gov/subjects/heritagedocumentation/copyright-guidance.htm
- Incidental historical artwork and merchandise in photographs: archive context.

steps.userMessage:
CROSSWATER | Short-trip commuter ferry cabin

Develop the complete enclosed passenger saloon of Ferry EUREKA, HAER CA-59, as a contemporary short-trip commuter cabin. The horizontal shell is fixed by the attached passenger-deck plan: the two transverse sliding-door partitions, four saloon openings, window-wall rhythm, columns, kingposts and central enclosures all stay in their recorded positions. The design covers both sides of the central bodies. Page-left is the Oakland end; page-right is the San Francisco end. These names provide cabin orientation. The exterior end decks retain their recorded stairs, railings and boundaries. Use the plan's original scale bar for horizontal dimensions, with 1 foot equal to 304.8 mm; identify traced values as approximate archive-derived dimensions. The 1988 photographs supply visible architectural relationships, and existing vertical dimensions remain unmeasured.

We need 120 seats in 60 two-person modules, 24 separately marked standing places and 12 bag positions numbered B01-B12. Each sitting surface is nominally 480 mm wide and 440 mm deep, at 450 mm above its local floor. Standing markers are nominally 550 by 550 mm, each served by a proposed handhold; the handhold system includes grasp surfaces at 950 mm and 1100 mm above the local floor. Each bag position accommodates an upright bag measuring 300 mm wide, 200 mm deep and 450 mm high. A continuous proposed 1200 mm clear circulation band connects all four opening approaches around both sides of the central bodies; the existing door throats retain their archived widths. Give commuters carrying bags a clear relationship between seats, standing places, storage and boarding order. Use recycled PET upholstery, aluminium supports and handholds, rubber bag-contact liners and floor surfaces, and printed aluminium information panels in a contemporary material system. Print "CROSSWATER" on the information surface of the fixed newsstand enclosure. Passenger wording is fixed as "Alight first", "Then board", "Seating", "Standing", "Bags", "Oakland end" and "San Francisco end".

Audience: the cabin design team and project owner, choosing the complete interior arrangement, material system and passenger information for further development.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the archive records, fixed shell features, furniture dimensions, passenger cases and wording. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists every deliverable with its proportion, format and stage. 03-archive-plan.png is the constraint image governing the horizontal shell, fixed objects, openings and scale. 04-archive-photo18.png is an identity image of the same vessel looking toward the newsstand, supplying visible architectural relationships. 05-archive-photo21.png is an identity image of the same vessel's athwartships passenger seating, supplying window, post and beam relationships. 06-waterfront-boarding-reference.png is an atmosphere reference for everyday waterfront passengers with commuter bags and a bicycle.

Deliverables:
1. A one-page hard-point and state sheet recording fixed shell features, the 120-seat and 24-standing-place targets, furniture dimensions, the 1200 mm circulation band, material assignments, passenger wording and CASE A and CASE B
2. One complete cabin plan with 60 numbered two-person modules, 24 numbered standing boxes, bag positions B01-B12, the circulation band, all four door approaches and section line A-A
3. One transverse relational section A-A through the open saloon between the Oakland-end partition and the newsstand, corresponding to the cabin plan, with new-element dimensions and the printed caption "Relational section; existing heights unmeasured"
4. One two-person seating-module detail with both sitting surfaces, support construction, material assignments and the 480 mm, 440 mm and 450 mm dimensions
5. One handhold-system detail identifying the 950 mm and 1100 mm grasp surfaces and the proposed hold serving each standing-place type
6. One bag-storage detail showing all 12 upright sample bags in B01-B12, each bag's 300 mm by 200 mm by 450 mm envelope, and the relationship to the circulation band
7. One material and colour system board covering seat contact, supports and handholds, bag contact, floor circulation cues and information panels, with named materials and colour codes
8. One passenger-information board containing the CROSSWATER newsstand panel, all seven fixed passenger labels, and the proposed locations of words, arrows and zone shapes
9. Two cabin perspectives, one toward the Oakland end and one toward the San Francisco end, located by viewing arrows on the cabin plan
10. One CASE A boarding sequence with two consecutive moments: three passengers leaving at the Oakland end under Alight first, followed by three passengers boarding under Then board
11. One CASE B riding scene with six seated passengers, two standing passengers using their proposed holds, and three bags in B01-B03
12. One 10-second passenger-sequence video progressing through CASE A and CASE B and reusing the cabin, furniture, materials and passenger wording
13. One presentation document of at least 8 pages, reusing the hard-point and state sheet, plan, section, details, material system, passenger information, perspectives and both passenger cases

Acceptance:
- The cabin plan establishes 60 two-person modules, 120 seats, 24 standing boxes and B01-B12; its dimensioned 1200 mm circulation band links all four door approaches around both sides of the central bodies. New furniture, standing boxes and bag positions sit outside the band, with archived door widths retained and door travel, fire-main positions and restroom/storage access visibly clear. The perspectives, passenger scenes and video retain this arrangement.
- The cabin plan, section A-A and two cabin perspectives preserve the boundary, openings, window rhythm and fixed objects recorded in 03-archive-plan.png. Section A-A matches its marked cut between the Oakland-end partition and newsstand, carries "Relational section; existing heights unmeasured", retains the visible window/post/beam relationships from the two archive photographs and dimensions the new furniture and holds.
- The seating detail repeats the state sheet's 480 mm sitting width, 440 mm depth and 450 mm height; the handhold detail repeats its 950 mm and 1100 mm grasp heights; the storage detail contains all 12 bags and their 300 mm by 200 mm by 450 mm envelopes. The presentation repeats these dimensions and the 1200 mm circulation target.
- The material board assigns recycled PET, aluminium and rubber to the surfaces named in the brief; the details, perspectives, scenes, video and presentation use those assignments and the board's colour codes. The information board, plan and scenes pair the Seating, Standing and Bags labels with distinct zone shapes, and the information board contains all seven fixed passenger labels. CROSSWATER appears on the newsstand panel in the information board, cabin perspectives and presentation.
- The CASE A sequence contains separate Alight first and Then board moments with three leaving and three boarding passengers respectively; the CASE B scene contains six seated passengers, two standing passengers holding their supports and three bags in B01-B03. The 10-second video and presentation repeat CASE A and CASE B, their passenger counts and their wording from the state sheet.
- The presentation has at least 8 pages and reuses every earlier deliverable category. One archive-credit entry records Historic American Engineering Record, National Park Service, Library of Congress; Dana Lockett, 1998, with source drawings Tri-Coastal / DePavloff Co., May 1990; and Jet Lowe, 1988, HAER CA-59-18 and CA-59-21, preserving the distinction between the plan and photograph dates.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
